public_rationale: A July autonomous-drone incident reportedly killed three civilians after the aircraft collided with a building. It is relevant evidence, but the accessible account does not conclusively identify an AI error or establish the prediction of errors costing many lives. The Airwars case predates the post and leaves AI involvement uncertain. No qualifying event settles the whole forecast. With no deadline, the absence of stronger evidence by October 28 is not a failure.
limitations: Public reporting may omit classified targeting and forensic information.
The strongest postpublication lead was accessible only through reporting about the original investigation.
No numerical meaning of many lives was imposed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Some military AI mistakes will cost lives, some many lives.

statement.excerpt: Some will cost lives, some will cost many lives.
statement.document_title: Is AI already killing people by accident?

our_interpretation: The forecast concerns military AI errors causing deaths after March 1, 2026.
Both fatal errors and errors causing clearly large losses of life must be established to support the whole claim.
Many lives has no supplied numerical threshold. A small number of deaths alone cannot establish the larger casualty component.
AI assistance in a lethal operation is insufficient by itself: an AI error must have contributed to the deaths.
criteria.support_condition: Credible investigations establish postpublication military AI mistakes causing deaths, including at least one incident with clearly numerous fatalities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Conclusive evidence rules out the predicted events over the forecast's entire scope. A finite period without a confirmed incident cannot contradict this undated forecast.

evidence.explanation: The report describes an autonomously guided drone hitting a building instead of its intended aim point and killing three civilians. This is relevant to the fatal-error component, but does not conclusively isolate an AI error or establish the larger casualty component; no primary forensic report was obtained.

evidence.locator: ‘No recognition, just misery’, paragraph following discussion of civilian harm assessments
evidence.explanation: Airwars documents a civilian death and inconsistent military statements about whether AI participated in the strike. The incident predates the forecast and does not establish that an AI mistake caused the death.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A credible investigation tying a postpublication incident with clearly numerous deaths to a specific military AI error would establish both components.
